u.write(b"${3:hello}\n")           # every byte is queued, never lossy

EVN drive base.description: Two motors as a Pybricks DriveBase (mm, deg clockwise)

EVN drive base drive.description: DriveBase: drive at a speed and turn rate until the next command

body: from evn import Motor, Direction, DriveBase, IMU, StopWatch, wait
left = Motor(${1:4}, Direction.COUNTERCLOCKWISE)   # the mirrored motor
imu = IMU(${3:3})                                   # fixed flat to the chassis; build it before the base
${6:db} = DriveBase(left, right, wheel_diameter=${4:62.4}, axle_track=${5:170}, imu=${3:3})   # the base builds its own Pose
while not imu.ready() and watch.time() < 30000:    # keep the robot still: the gyro calibrates 8-25 s in
${6:db}.use_gyro(True)     # the robot follows the path, not just the wheels
EVN drive base follows its gyro.description: DriveBase with imu= builds and owns its evn.Pose (encoders + IMU) and closes the loop over it: scrub, drag and gyro drift corrected as the robot drives

body: from evn import Motor, IMU, DataLog
${3:log} = DataLog(name='${4:run1}')   # recorded on the board, in RAM: 32 kB by default (size=)
${3:log}.add(motor, 'angle')          # 0 = every new reading (up to 1000 a second)
${3:log}.add(imu, 'heading', ${5:50})     # samples a second; a full channel halves its rate
motor.stop()                       # save() is refused (OSError EBUSY) while a motor drives
EVN data log.description: evn.DataLog: record motors and sensors on the board at their own rates, then save a CSV once the motors coast
